page.overview:
Who is Dambala?

Dambala was a skilled reptile handler affiliated with Dr. Kananga's voodoo cult. A minor villain, the character first appeared in the 1973 James Bond film Live and Let Die, portrayed by the late Bermudian actor Michael Ebbin, and was also seen in the James Bond 007 tabletop role-playing game.

Dambala is the chief of a tribe living on the fictional island of San Monique, which is governed by Kananga, who is secretly behind the appearances of Dambala's god, Baron Samedi, who he needs to use to get Dambala to eliminate his enemies via sacrifices to Baron Samedi. We see one such sacrifice at the end of the pre-titles sequence: MI6 agent Baines is tied to an altar, being menaced with a venomous snake by Dambala as the rest of the tribe dance as part of their strange ritual. Eventually, Dambala throws blood over Baines, and then holds the snake in his face, causing it to bite him to death.

Later in the film, Kananga's unfaithful medium Solitaire is condemned to the same fate. Bound by her wrists between two stakes, she watches as a coffin is brought into the field. Dambala emerges from behind a gravestone, approaches the casket and lifts the lid, revealing a heaving mass of venomous snakes. After selecting the one that killed the unfortunate Baines, he raises it aloft and carries it towards the helpless Solitaire, taunting her with its lethal fangs. However, as he moves in to administer the fatal bite, the ceremony is halted, so that the absent Baron Samedi can be summoned. After Samedi rises from the grave (in the form of a statue) and gives the signal to proceed, Dambala races back towards to Solitaire to sacrifice her, but James Bond shoots him before he can do it, avenging Baines' death.
